title: Each merge makes every waiting change gate again
what: When several ready changes wait, each merge puts the others behind master; each must take master, gate again (~10 min) and get a checker, one after another. Find the cheapest safe order: e.g. a merge train (take master once into the last change after the others merged and gate only the combined head), or skip the re-gate when master's new commits and the branch share no file and the earlier gate covered both sides (a fact code can check), and keep the combined-by-merge check only for files both sides changed.
why: 24 Oct: four changes were ready at once (py-rule, installer, checks-record, paid-batch); every merge forced the next ones to take master, gate and check again, about 10-15 agent minutes and one runner + one checker per change per merge; the same day checks-record took master three times. Principle 2: waste built into the setup.
failing_case: 24 Oct: after py-rule merged, paid-batch (no shared file but tests/test_relay.py) had to gate again before its merge; checks-record will gate a fourth time after paid-batch merges.
pass_cases: With N ready changes, the rules and hook let them merge with at most one extra gate in total, or skip it when code shows no overlap; a merge whose branch and master's new commits share a file still gets the combined-by-merge check and a gate.
where: rules/git.md (ready to merge), plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md, plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md step 8, plugins/core/hooks/merge.py
